title: start_run test drives seed_fixture through a silently-swallowed catalog miss: the content_host lookup falls back to type index 0 (residential)
detail: The new test drives start_run on a catalog missing content_host; the miss path is unguarded and silent, so the driven boot topology diverges from production (mis-typed host node feeding the home centroid). Asserts still pass; fidelity issue only.
recommended_fix: Append a content_host Node_Type in the test before start_run, or assert the lookup: `host_idx, ok := pp.node_type_index(...); testing.expect(t, ok, ...)`. Alternatively note the divergence in the test comment.

title: The hunk comment misattributes start_run's pullback clear to the destroy-then-reinit; the only clear on that path is the camera_set_default routing call itself
evidence:
Diff comment: `NOTE: start_run clears pullback
via its destroy-then-reinit run-init independent of the camera routing, so
start_run_wiring_homes_on_the_source_cluster pins ONLY the routing`. But grep of start_run's body (main.odin:874-988) finds zero `pullback` references except the camera_set_default call; run_destroy is Run_State-scoped: `run_destroy :: proc(state: ^Run_State)` and never touches App.pullback; the clear lives only in camera_set_default (main.odin:1759-1765): `camera_set_default :: proc(app: ^App) {
	app.cam_wx_to = app.home_wx
	app.cam_wy_to = app.home_wy
	app.cam_zoom_to = rnd.DEFAULT_ZOOM
	app.pullback = false`.
detail: The comment's mechanism claim is false: removing the start_run routing call leaves an armed pullback stale across restart, because run_destroy/run_init never reset App.pullback. Coverage is still safe (home-target asserts go red), but the rationale documented is wrong.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment: the clear rides the camera_set_default routing call (transitively pinned by the routing asserts); the reinit does not reset App.pullback. Optionally arm pullback=true and assert the clear.
